scenario: ML 系统设计面试中，面试官在你画完架构后追问「如果训练数据砍掉 90% 呢？」或「你为什么用 Kafka 而不是 Kinesis？」。
scenario_en: In an ML system design interview, after you finish the architecture the interviewer asks 'what if training data shrinks 90%?' or 'why Kafka instead of Kinesis?'
q: MAANG 面试的 pushback 主要分哪两类，各测什么？
q_en: What are the two main kinds of MAANG interview pushback, and what does each test?
why: 两类：constraint injection 改一个参数（规模/延迟/数据量），测你能不能不推倒重来地适应；decision challenge 质疑某个具体选择，测你懂不懂那个取舍、还是随手默认选的。先判断是哪类，回应方式才对。
why_en: Constraint injection changes a parameter to test if you adapt without starting over, while decision challenge questions a specific choice to test whether you understand its tradeoff.

rows: 一个参数(规模/延迟/数据)

options: 语法性问题 vs 事实性问题：一类问你术语拼写，一类问你背没背过定义
简单题 vs 难题：一类送分暖场，一类专门为难你想让你答不出
constraint injection(改一个参数看你能否适应) vs decision challenge(质疑某选择看你懂不懂取舍)
技术问题 vs 行为问题：一类问系统设计，一类问你过去的项目经历
options_en: Syntax questions vs fact questions: one asks you to spell a term, one asks you to recite a definition.
Easy vs hard: one is a warm-up freebie, one is designed to stump you so you can't answer.
Constraint injection (changes a parameter to see if you adapt) vs decision challenge (questions a choice to see if you grasp the tradeoff).
Technical vs behavioral: one asks about system design, one asks about your past projects.
optionExplanations: 面试 pushback 不是考拼写或背定义，把它当知识默写就答偏了方向。
把 pushback 当刁难是最危险的心态误读——它其实是在测你的边界和适应力，不是想让你出丑。
对；识别是「改约束」还是「质疑选择」，才知道该走 4 步适配还是该讲清当初的取舍轴。
行为面试是另一种轮次，这里两类 pushback 都发生在技术设计的追问里。
optionExplanations_en: Interview pushback isn't testing spelling or memorized definitions; treating it as recall aims at the wrong thing.
Reading pushback as harassment is the most dangerous misread — it actually tests your boundaries and adaptability, not tries to embarrass you.
Correct — telling 'changed constraint' from 'questioned choice' tells you whether to run the 4-step adaptation or to explain your original tradeoff axis.
Behavioral is a different round; here both pushback kinds happen inside technical design follow-ups.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面试官改动一个参数(规模/延迟/数据量)，看你能否在原设计上适应而非推倒重来。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Constraint injection is when the interviewer changes a parameter (scale, latency, data) to see if you adapt your design rather than restart.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面试官质疑你某个具体技术选择，看你是否真的理解那个取舍。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Decision challenge is when the interviewer questions a specific technical choice to see if you truly understand the tradeoff.

termDefinitions.meaning: 指 Meta/Amazon/Apple/Netflix/Google 一类大厂，面试节奏和考点相近。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MAANG refers to big-tech firms like Meta, Amazon, Apple, Netflix, and Google with similar interview styles.

scenario: 面试官突然把 p99 延迟要求从 200ms 收紧到 50ms，候选人心里一慌，以为自己整个设计被否了。
scenario_en: The interviewer suddenly tightens p99 latency from 200ms to 50ms; the candidate panics, assuming the whole design was rejected.
q: 面试官频繁 pushback 说明什么，正确心态是什么？
q_en: What does frequent pushback signal, and what's the right mindset?
why: pushback 是刻意的，测的是 adaptability、depth 和 composure；追问 = 对你的边界感兴趣，不是说你错了。把它当危机、进入防御状态，才是真正的失分点。
why_en: Pushback is deliberate — it tests adaptability, depth, and composure, so engagement means interest in your boundaries, not that you're wrong.
options: 说明设计被否了，应立刻推倒重画一个全新架构证明你会别的方案
说明面试官对你的边界感兴趣，是刻意测 adaptability/depth/composure，不代表你错了
说明面试官没听懂你的设计，应该把刚才的方案再从头讲一遍讲得更细
说明时间快到了，面试官在用难题快速结束这一轮
options_en: It means the design was rejected; immediately scrap it and draw a brand-new architecture to prove you know alternatives.
It means the interviewer is interested in your boundaries, deliberately testing adaptability/depth/composure — not that you're wrong.
It means the interviewer didn't understand your design; re-explain the whole thing from the top in more detail.
It means time is nearly up and the interviewer is using a hard question to end the round quickly.
optionExplanations: 一被 push 就推倒重来，暴露的恰恰是没主见、扛不住追问，比坚持一个可调整的设计信号更差。
对；pushback 是设计好的探针，测你能不能冷静适应、往深了走，engagement 是兴趣不是判决。
重复讲一遍解决不了追问，面试官要的是你对新约束的反应，不是更详细的旧答案。
追问恰恰是想让你多展示，不是想草草收尾；把它读成时间信号会错过发挥机会。
optionExplanations_en: Scrapping everything on the first push reveals exactly the lack of conviction, worse signal than adapting a design you can defend.
Correct — pushback is a designed probe testing calm adaptation and depth; engagement is interest, not a verdict.
Re-explaining doesn't address the follow-up; the interviewer wants your reaction to the new constraint, not a longer old answer.
The follow-up wants more from you, not a quick wrap-up; reading it as a time signal wastes the chance to shine.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面对追问保持冷静、结构化回应的能力，是面试官明确在观察的信号之一。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Composure is staying calm and structured under follow-ups, one of the signals the interviewer explicitly watches for.

termDefinitions.meaning: 99% 的请求延迟都低于这个值，衡量尾部延迟；比平均值更能反映最差用户体验。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: p99 latency is the value under which 99% of requests fall, measuring tail latency and worst-case user experience better than the average.

q: 把回应 pushback 的 4 步框架排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order the 4-step pushback-response framework correctly:
steps: Assess impact：沿请求路径扫一遍，点名哪些具体组件会坏
Confirm alignment：问「这个方向对吗」，避免优化面试官没想要的路径
Acknowledge：用自己的话复述约束，证明理解并争取思考时间
Propose adaptation：说清什么变、什么不变，明确取舍与迁移路径
why: 顺序是先复述约束(Acknowledge)→再点名受影响组件(Assess)→提出带取舍的适配(Propose)→最后对齐方向(Confirm)。先理解再动手，最后确认，避免精修一条面试官根本没想要的路。
why_en: Acknowledge the constraint, assess which components break, propose an adaptation with tradeoffs, then confirm alignment so you don't optimize a path the interviewer never intended.
diagram:
flowchart LR A["1 Acknowledge
复述约束"] --> B["2 Assess impact
点名坏掉的组件"] B --> C["3 Propose adaptation
什么变/不变+取舍"] C --> D["4 Confirm alignment
方向对吗"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 第一步：用自己的话把新约束说一遍，既证明听懂又争取到几秒思考时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Acknowledge is step one: restate the new constraint in your own words to prove understanding and buy thinking time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 第四步：问面试官方向对不对，防止你深入优化一条对方没想要的路径。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Confirm alignment is step four: ask if the direction matches, preventing you from optimizing a path the interviewer didn't intend.

scenario: 面试官刚把约束改了（「延迟预算砍半」），你脑子里已经想直接跳去改 embedding 维度。
scenario_en: The interviewer just changed a constraint ('latency budget halved') and you're tempted to jump straight to cutting embedding dimensions.
q: 4 步法第一步该先做什么，为什么？
q_en: What's the first step of the 4-step framework, and why?
why: 先 Acknowledge：用自己的话复述约束（「所以 p99 要从 200 降到 50ms」）。这既证明你真听懂了，又给自己争取几秒结构化思考的时间，避免慌忙乱改。
why_en: Acknowledge first: restate the constraint in your own words, which both proves you understood and buys a few seconds of structured thinking time.
tradeoff: 先复述约束(证明理解+争取时间) vs 直接动手改(可能改错方向、显慌乱)
options: 先 Acknowledge：用自己的话复述约束，证明理解并争取几秒思考时间
先跳到改设计：立刻把 embedding 维度砍一半，用速度证明你反应快
先反问面试官为什么要改这个约束，让对方先解释清楚再说
先沉默 30 秒把完整新方案在脑子里想全，想好了再一口气讲完
options_en: Acknowledge first: restate the constraint in your own words to prove understanding and buy a few seconds.
Jump to redesign: immediately halve the embedding dimension to prove you react fast.
Ask the interviewer why they changed this constraint and make them explain before you respond.
Go silent for 30 seconds to fully work out the new solution in your head, then deliver it all at once.
whenOtherWins: 如果约束的措辞本身有歧义（如「更快」没给具体数字），先短问一句澄清目标值是合理的，但确认后仍要复述再往下走。
whenOtherWins_en: If the constraint's wording is genuinely ambiguous (e.g. 'faster' with no number), a brief clarifying question is fine, but you still restate before proceeding.
optionExplanations: 对；复述是低成本高回报的一步，锁住理解、争取时间，也把讨论钉在同一个约束上。
不复述直接改，容易改错方向又显得慌；快不等于对，面试官要的是结构不是抢答。
把「你为什么改」直接甩回给面试官显得抵触；4 步法里质疑约束正是要避免的防御姿态。
沉默 30 秒把全套想完再开口太久，正确做法是边复述边结构化，让思考过程可见。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — restating is low-cost, high-return: it locks in understanding, buys time, and anchors the discussion on the same constraint.
Editing without restating risks the wrong direction and looks panicked; fast isn't right, and the interviewer wants structure, not a buzzer race.
Throwing 'why did you change it' back at the interviewer reads as resistant; arguing the constraint is exactly the defensive posture to avoid.
30 seconds of silence before speaking is too long; the right move is to restate while structuring so your thinking stays visible.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把内容编码成的稠密向量长度，维度越高表达力越强但存储、检索、推理越贵。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Embedding dimension is the length of the dense vector encoding content; higher means more expressive but costlier to store, index, and serve.

scenario: 约束变了（p99 从 200ms 收紧到 50ms），你要评估这对现有两阶段推荐设计的冲击。
scenario_en: The constraint changed (p99 tightened 200ms to 50ms) and you must assess the impact on your existing two-stage recommender.
q: Assess impact 这一步，点名具体组件还是泛泛描述影响？
q_en: In the assess-impact step, name specific components or describe the impact generally?
why: 沿请求路径从用户动作走到模型响应，点名会坏的具体组件——远程 feature store 的实时特征查询、重 reranking 阶段——而不是泛泛一句「延迟会上升」。具体定位才让下一步适配有的放矢。
why_en: Walk the request path from user action to model response and name the specific components that break (remote feature lookup, heavy reranking), not a vague 'latency goes up'.
tradeoff: 点名具体组件(可定位、可适配) vs 泛泛说影响(听着像没真懂系统)
diagram:
flowchart LR U["用户请求"] --> F["远程 feature store
实时特征查询 ← 慢"] F --> R["候选生成"] R --> RK["重 reranking ← 贵"] RK --> O["响应"]
options: 泛泛说「延迟会整体上升、成本会变高」，具体组件留到面试官追问再说
沿请求路径点名具体会坏的组件：远程实时特征查询、重 reranking 阶段
直接说整个设计都得推倒，因为新延迟约束下什么都不满足
只报一个数字「现在 200ms，要 50ms」，不分析是哪部分耗了这 200ms
options_en: Say vaguely 'latency rises and cost goes up overall,' leaving specific components until the interviewer probes.
Walk the request path and name the specific components that break: remote real-time feature lookup, heavy reranking stage.
Say the whole design must be scrapped because nothing meets the new latency constraint.
Just report a number '200ms now, need 50ms' without analyzing which part spends the 200ms.
whenOtherWins: 如果系统很简单、只有单个同步模型调用，那「延迟主要在模型推理」就是准确定位，不必硬拆多组件——但复杂管线必须逐段点名。
whenOtherWins_en: If the system is simple with a single synchronous model call, 'latency is dominated by inference' is precise enough, but a complex pipeline must be broken down component by component.
optionExplanations: 泛泛描述等于没定位，面试官听不出你懂不懂这条请求路径，也没法引出针对性适配。
对；走一遍请求路径、点名远程特征查询和重 reranking，证明你真懂系统在哪耗时。
「全推倒」是过度反应，新约束通常只压垮少数几个组件，不需要全盘重来。
只报数字不拆解，等于承认不知道 200ms 花在哪，下一步适配也就无从下手。
optionExplanations_en: A vague description locates nothing; the interviewer can't tell if you know the request path and can't derive a targeted fix.
Correct — walking the path and naming the remote lookup and heavy reranking proves you know where the system spends time.
'Scrap everything' overreacts; a new constraint usually crushes only a few components, not the whole design.
Reporting only the number without breaking it down admits you don't know where the 200ms goes, leaving no basis to adapt.

termDefinitions.meaning: 集中存储、按需提供模型特征的系统；实时查询远程 feature store 会在请求路径上加延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A feature store centrally stores and serves model features; a real-time remote lookup adds latency on the request path.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两阶段检索的第二阶段，用更重的模型给候选精细打分排序，通常是最耗算力的一步。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Reranking is the second stage of two-stage retrieval, finely scoring candidates with a heavier model, usually the most compute-heavy step.

scenario: 评估完约束冲击，你要向面试官提出适配方案（Propose adaptation）。
scenario_en: Having assessed the impact, you're about to propose an adaptation to the interviewer.
q: 一个到位的「Propose adaptation」该包含哪些要素？(多选)
q_en: What should a strong 'propose adaptation' step include? (multiple)
why: 要素：说清什么变、什么不变；显式点名取舍（「牺牲个性化深度，换到延迟 SLO」）；给出可逆性/迁移路径。缺哪个都显得没想全。反过来去论证约束不合理，是要避免的防御姿态。
why_en: Name what changes and what stays, state the tradeoff explicitly, and give a reversibility or migration path; arguing the constraint is invalid is the posture to avoid.
options: 说清什么组件变、什么保持不变
显式点名取舍：牺牲了什么，换到了什么
给出可逆性/迁移路径：约束放松后怎么回到原设计
论证这个约束不现实，说服面试官把它撤回
options_en: Name what components change and what stays the same.
State the tradeoff explicitly: what you give up and what you gain.
Give a reversibility / migration path: how to return to the original design once the constraint relaxes.
Argue the constraint is unrealistic and persuade the interviewer to withdraw it.
optionExplanations: 对；「什么变/什么不变」让面试官看到你是有选择地改，不是慌乱全盘推翻。
对；不点名取舍等于假装免费午餐，资深信号恰恰是同口气说出代价。
对；补一句迁移路径是高分细节，证明你把方案当可演进的工程而非一次性补丁。
错；跟约束较劲是 defensive spiral，会丢信任——约束是给定的，你要适应不是推翻。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — 'what changes vs stays' shows the interviewer you edit selectively, not panic-scrap everything.
Correct — skipping the tradeoff pretends there's a free lunch; the senior signal is stating the cost in the same breath.
Correct — adding a migration path is a high-scoring detail, showing you treat the design as evolvable, not a one-off patch.
Wrong — fighting the constraint is a defensive spiral that loses trust; the constraint is given, you adapt rather than overturn it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个改动能否在约束放松后回退到原设计，体现方案是可演进而非一次性补丁。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Reversibility is whether a change can be rolled back to the original design once the constraint relaxes, showing the plan is evolvable.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务级目标，如「p99 延迟 < 50ms」，是给定的工程目标而非可推导数字。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SLO (Service-Level Objective) is a target like 'p99 latency < 50ms', a given engineering goal rather than a derived number.

scenario: 你提完了适配方案（砍 embedding 维度、缩候选集），正想接着深入优化 reranking 的细节。
scenario_en: You've proposed the adaptation (cut embedding dim, shrink candidate set) and are about to dive deep into reranking details.
q: 4 步法最后一步为什么要 Confirm alignment？
q_en: Why is the final step, confirm alignment, important?
why: 问一句「这个方向和你想的一致吗？」能防止你花大量时间精修一条面试官根本没打算走的路径。对齐是低成本的纠偏点，越往深走越贵。
why_en: Asking 'does this direction match what you had in mind?' prevents you from deeply optimizing a path the interviewer never intended.
tradeoff: 先确认方向(便宜纠偏) vs 闷头深入优化(可能整段白做)
options: 为了显得礼貌，让面试官觉得你尊重他的意见
为了拖时间，把剩下的面试时长用问句填满
为了防止你深入优化一条面试官根本没想要的路径，对齐是便宜的纠偏点
为了把责任推给面试官，出了问题可以说是他同意的方向
options_en: To seem polite and make the interviewer feel respected.
To stall for time and fill the remaining minutes with questions.
To prevent deeply optimizing a path the interviewer never intended — alignment is a cheap correction point.
To shift responsibility to the interviewer so you can blame them if it goes wrong.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官已经明确点头认可了方向，就不必反复确认，直接往深里做——过度 confirm 会显得缺乏主见。
whenOtherWins_en: If the interviewer has clearly endorsed the direction, don't keep re-confirming — over-checking reads as lacking conviction; just go deep.
optionExplanations: 礼貌是副产品不是目的，confirm 的真正价值是纠偏，不是社交表演。
拖时间是负信号，confirm 是一句话的快速核对，不是用来填时长的。
对；越往深走成本越高，花一句话确认方向能避免整段优化白做。
confirm 是协作对齐不是甩锅，把它当免责声明会读出不担当。
optionExplanations_en: Politeness is a byproduct, not the point; confirm's real value is course-correction, not social performance.
Stalling is a negative signal; confirm is a one-line quick check, not filler.
Correct — the deeper you go the costlier, so one line confirming direction avoids wasting a whole optimization pass.
Confirm is collaborative alignment, not blame-shifting; treating it as a disclaimer reads as ducking ownership.

termDefinitions.meaning: 提完适配后主动问面试官方向对不对，在深入前做一次便宜的纠偏。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Confirm alignment means asking the interviewer if your direction is right before diving deep, a cheap course-correction.

scenario: 两塔推荐系统，serving 预算被砍半。当前 embedding 维度和候选集大小让推理成本超预算。
scenario_en: A two-tower recommender whose serving budget is halved; the current embedding dimension and candidate-set size push inference cost over budget.
q: 预算砍半时，最该动哪两个旋钮来把成本压回预算内？
q_en: With budget halved, which two knobs do you turn to fit cost back in budget?
why: ANN 索引和 reranking 是两个最贵的组件：把 embedding 维度 256→128、reranking 候选集 500→200。代价是冷门 query 的 recall 略降，但热门 item 的核心检索质量保住，正好压回预算。
why_en: ANN index and reranking are the two costliest parts: cut embedding dim 256→128 and reranking candidate set 500→200, trading niche-query recall for staying in budget while keeping core quality.
tradeoff: 砍维度+缩候选集(省算力、保热门质量) vs 保持不变(质量高但超预算)
options: 把 embedding 维度 256→128、reranking 候选集 500→200，牺牲冷门 recall 保热门质量
把训练数据量翻倍，让模型更准就能自然变快、抵消预算压力
换更大的 GPU 实例把吞吐拉满，用硬件堆过预算约束
把整个 reranking 阶段删掉，只靠候选生成直接出结果
options_en: Cut embedding dim 256→128 and reranking candidate set 500→200, trading niche recall to keep popular-item quality.
Double the training data so a more accurate model naturally gets faster and offsets the budget pressure.
Switch to bigger GPU instances to max throughput, brute-forcing past the budget constraint.
Delete the entire reranking stage and serve candidate-generation output directly.
whenOtherWins: 如果冷门/长尾 query 恰恰是产品核心价值（如利基电商），就不能砍到伤 recall，得改从其它组件（如缓存、蒸馏）省成本。
whenOtherWins_en: If long-tail queries are the product's core value (e.g. niche e-commerce), don't cut into recall — save cost elsewhere via caching or distillation instead.
optionExplanations: 对；维度和候选集是成本的两个主旋钮，按比例调小直接压成本，代价可控且可解释。
加训练数据只影响离线训练成本，不降 serving 单次推理成本，方向搞反了。
换更大 GPU 是加钱不是省钱，预算砍半的约束下堆硬件正好违背要求。
整段删 reranking 会大幅掉精度，是过度反应；缩小候选集就够而不必砍掉整层。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — dimension and candidate set are the two main cost knobs; scaling them down directly cuts cost with a controllable, explainable tradeoff.
More training data affects offline training cost, not per-request serving cost, so it's the wrong direction.
Bigger GPUs spend more, not less; brute-forcing hardware under a halved budget directly violates the constraint.
Deleting reranking wholesale tanks precision — an overreaction; shrinking the candidate set suffices without removing the stage.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户塔和物品塔各自编码成向量，用向量相似度做候选检索的经典推荐架构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A two-tower model encodes user and item into separate vectors and retrieves candidates by vector similarity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应被检索到的相关结果里实际被检索到的比例，检索质量的核心指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Recall is the fraction of relevant items that were actually retrieved, the core retrieval-quality metric.

termDefinitions.meaning: 近似最近邻检索，在海量向量里快速找相似向量，牺牲一点精度换大幅提速。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ANN (Approximate Nearest Neighbor) quickly finds similar vectors in a huge set, trading a little accuracy for large speedups.

scenario: 面试官注入约束：规模 +100x。当前检索用 brute-force 逐个比对，一下子扛不住了。
scenario_en: Constraint injected: scale +100x. The current retrieval brute-forces every item and can't keep up.
q: 规模 +100x 让检索成瓶颈，该怎么适配？
q_en: Scale +100x makes retrieval the bottleneck — how do you adapt?
why: 检索成瓶颈时，把 brute-force 换成 ANN 近似检索，再加一个轻量预过滤先砍掉明显不相关的候选。代价是 recall 略降，但延迟和成本被 ANN 的次线性检索约束住。
why_en: When retrieval bottlenecks, swap brute-force for ANN and add a lightweight pre-filter, trading slight recall for bounded latency and cost.
tradeoff: ANN+预过滤(次线性、可扩展、略掉recall) vs brute-force(精确但随规模线性爆炸)
options: brute-force → ANN 近似检索 + 轻量预过滤先砍候选；recall 略降但延迟/成本有界
保持 brute-force，只是把它并行到更多机器上，规模问题用横向复制解决
把检索和排序合并成一个大模型，一次算完就不用分两阶段扛规模了
缓存所有历史检索结果，新请求直接查缓存不再实时检索
options_en: Brute-force → ANN retrieval + a lightweight pre-filter to cut candidates first; recall dips slightly but latency/cost are bounded.
Keep brute-force, just parallelize it across more machines — solve scale by horizontal replication.
Merge retrieval and ranking into one big model so it's computed once and doesn't split into two stages.
Cache all historical retrieval results so new requests hit the cache instead of retrieving live.
whenOtherWins: 如果目录其实不大（几万条以内），brute-force 精确检索反而更简单可靠，不必上 ANN 增加索引维护复杂度。
whenOtherWins_en: If the catalog is actually small (tens of thousands), exact brute-force is simpler and more reliable — no need for ANN's index-maintenance complexity.
optionExplanations: 对；ANN 把检索从线性降到近似次线性，加预过滤进一步减负，是规模爆炸的标准解。
brute-force 是每 item 都比对，规模 +100x 成本也 +100x，堆机器只是把线性爆炸摊开，没治本。
合并成一个大模型给全量打分，正是规模下跑不动的原因，两阶段拆分才是为扛规模。
缓存对个性化实时检索几乎无用——每个用户/上下文不同，命中率极低，救不了检索瓶颈。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — ANN drops retrieval from linear to near-sublinear, and a pre-filter cuts further; the standard answer to scale explosion.
Brute-force compares every item, so +100x scale means +100x cost; adding machines just spreads the linear blow-up without fixing it.
Merging into one big model to score everything is exactly what can't run at scale; the two-stage split exists to handle scale.
Caching barely helps personalized live retrieval — each user/context differs, so hit rate is tiny and it won't fix the bottleneck.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把 query 和每一个候选逐个比对相似度，精确但成本随目录大小线性增长。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Brute-force retrieval compares the query against every candidate, exact but with cost linear in catalog size.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在重检索前用轻量规则先砍掉明显不相关的候选，减小后续计算量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A pre-filter uses light rules to drop obviously irrelevant candidates before heavy retrieval, shrinking downstream compute.

scenario: 面试官把延迟预算砍半。当前设计有一个重 reranking 阶段和多个实时特征查询，正是耗时大头。
scenario_en: The interviewer halves the latency budget; the design has a heavy reranking stage and several real-time feature lookups that dominate the time.
q: 延迟预算砍半，重 reranking 和实时特征是瓶颈，怎么适配？
q_en: Latency budget halved, heavy reranking and real-time features bottleneck — how do you adapt?
why: 把实时特征改成离线批量预计算、缩小候选集、对排序模型做蒸馏得到更小更快的版本。代价是尾部 query 的精度可能下降，但主路径能进新延迟预算。
why_en: Precompute features in batch, shrink the candidate set, and distill the ranker into a smaller faster model, trading tail-query accuracy for meeting the new latency budget.
tradeoff: 预计算+缩候选+蒸馏(快、尾部精度略降) vs 保持重排(准但超延迟预算)
options: 把延迟预算的数字告诉运维，让他们升级网络带宽把延迟降下来
把所有特征都实时计算得更精确，精度上去了自然就不卡了
给用户加一个 loading 动画，让 200ms 感觉起来像 50ms
实时特征改批量预计算 + 缩小候选集 + 排序模型蒸馏；代价是尾部 query 精度可能降
options_en: Tell ops the latency number and have them upgrade network bandwidth to bring latency down.
Compute all features in real time more precisely; higher accuracy will naturally remove the lag.
Add a loading animation so 200ms feels like 50ms to the user.
Move real-time features to batch precompute + shrink candidate set + distill the ranker; cost is possible tail-query accuracy drop.
whenOtherWins: 如果延迟大头其实在网络往返而非计算（如跨地域调用），那减少远程调用/就近部署才是对的，蒸馏模型救不了 RTT。
whenOtherWins_en: If latency is dominated by network round-trips (e.g. cross-region calls) rather than compute, reducing remote calls or co-locating is the fix — distillation can't cut RTT.
optionExplanations: 带宽不是这里的瓶颈——延迟花在特征计算和重排序上，升级网络对计算延迟无效。
实时算更多特征只会更慢，方向反了；延迟约束要减计算量不是加计算量。
动画是感知欺骗，模型分数照样迟到；面试考的是真延迟不是 UI 障眼法。
对；预计算移走实时开销、缩候选减排序量、蒸馏压小模型，三招直接压延迟，代价说清是尾部精度。
optionExplanations_en: Bandwidth isn't the bottleneck here — latency is spent on feature compute and reranking, so a network upgrade won't touch compute latency.
Computing more features in real time is slower, the wrong direction; a latency constraint needs less compute, not more.
An animation is perceptual trickery; the model's scores still arrive late, and the interview tests real latency, not UI sleight of hand.

Correct — precompute removes real-time cost, a smaller candidate set cuts ranking work, and distillation shrinks the model; three moves that directly cut latency with tail accuracy as the stated cost.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用大模型(teacher)的输出训练一个小模型(student)，保住大部分精度但推理更快更省。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Model distillation trains a small student model on a large teacher's outputs, keeping most accuracy while running faster and cheaper.

termDefinitions.meaning: 提前离线把特征算好存起来，请求时直接查而不在请求路径上现算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Batch precompute calculates features offline ahead of time so requests read them instead of computing on the request path.

scenario: 面试官注入约束：训练数据砍掉 90%。你原本用的是一个大深度模型，特征覆盖也依赖大数据量。
scenario_en: Constraint injected: training data shrinks 90%. You were using a large deep model whose feature coverage relies on data volume.
q: 训练数据 −90%，深度模型要过拟合了，怎么适配？
q_en: Training data −90%, the deep model will overfit — how do you adapt?
why: 数据剧减时深模型容量太大会过拟合：换成更简单的模型（如梯度提升树 GBT）、用迁移学习借外部预训练、加正则。代价是对复杂特征交互的建模能力下降，但在小数据上更稳。
why_en: With data slashed, a high-capacity deep model overfits: switch to a simpler model (GBT), use transfer learning, and add regularization, trading complex-interaction capacity for stability on small data.
tradeoff: 简单模型+迁移+正则(小数据稳、少建复杂交互) vs 大深模型(表达强但小数据必过拟合)
options: 坚持用原深度模型，只是把 epoch 数调大反复训练把少量数据榨干
换更简单的模型(GBT) + 迁移学习借预训练 + 加正则；代价是复杂交互建模能力下降
用剩下 10% 数据合成 10 倍假数据凑回原规模，继续按大数据训练
把模型参数量再翻倍，让它记住这少量数据的每个细节
options_en: Keep the original deep model, just raise the epoch count to squeeze the little data by training repeatedly.
Switch to a simpler model (GBT) + transfer learning from pretraining + regularization; cost is less capacity for complex interactions.
Synthesize 10x fake data from the remaining 10% to restore scale and keep training as if data were large.
Double the model's parameter count so it memorizes every detail of the small dataset.
whenOtherWins: 如果那 10% 数据其实还很大（原本是超大规模），或有强预训练可微调，深度模型仍可行，不必退回到 GBT。
whenOtherWins_en: If the remaining 10% is still large (originally massive scale), or a strong pretrained model can be fine-tuned, a deep model stays viable without falling back to GBT.
optionExplanations: 小数据反复多训只会加剧过拟合——模型背下噪声，泛化更差，epoch 调大是火上浇油。
对；降容量(GBT)、借外部知识(迁移)、压过拟合(正则)三管齐下，是小数据的标准处方。
凭空合成 10 倍数据会灌进虚假分布，模型学到的是合成 artifact 不是真实信号。
参数翻倍在小数据上是反向操作——容量越大越容易死记硬背，过拟合更严重。
optionExplanations_en: Training small data harder just worsens overfitting — the model memorizes noise and generalizes worse; more epochs pour fuel on the fire.
Correct — lower capacity (GBT), borrow external knowledge (transfer), and curb overfit (regularization): the standard small-data prescription.
Fabricating 10x data injects a fake distribution; the model learns synthesis artifacts, not real signal.
Doubling parameters on small data is backwards — more capacity means more rote memorization and worse overfitting.

termDefinitions.meaning: 梯度提升树，串联多棵浅决策树的经典模型；在中小结构化数据上稳、不易过拟合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GBT (Gradient-Boosted Trees) chains shallow decision trees; robust and hard to overfit on small-to-mid structured data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 借用在大数据上预训练好的模型或表征，微调到本任务，缓解本地数据不足。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Transfer learning reuses representations pretrained on large data and fine-tunes them to the task, easing local data scarcity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型记住训练数据的噪声细节，在新数据上泛化差；数据越少、模型越大越严重。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Overfitting is when a model memorizes training noise and generalizes poorly; worse with less data and bigger models.

scenario: 面试官注入约束：新法规(GDPR)生效，不能再用用户级个人特征。你原设计重度依赖用户历史画像。
scenario_en: Constraint injected: new regulation (GDPR) takes effect and user-level personal features are off-limits. Your design leaned heavily on per-user profiles.
q: GDPR 让用户级特征不可用，怎么适配还能保留推荐能力？
q_en: GDPR makes user-level features unavailable — how do you adapt while keeping recommendations working?
why: 改用不依赖个人身份的信号：上下文特征（时段、设备、当前内容）、cohort/群体信号（同类用户聚合）、以及把推理放到端上(on-device)让数据不出设备。代价是个性化变浅，但合规。
why_en: Switch to non-identifying signals: contextual features, cohort-level signals, and on-device inference so data stays local, trading personalization depth for compliance.
tradeoff: 上下文+cohort+端上推理(合规、个性化变浅) vs 用户级画像(个性化深但违规)
options: 把用户特征加密后照常使用，反正加密了就不算个人数据了
改用上下文特征 + cohort 群体信号 + on-device 端上推理；代价是个性化变浅但合规
无视法规继续用用户画像，等被投诉了再改，先把系统跑起来
把所有用户数据搬到没有 GDPR 的地区服务器，绕开监管
options_en: Encrypt the user features and use them as usual — once encrypted they no longer count as personal data.
Switch to contextual features + cohort signals + on-device inference; cost is shallower personalization but compliance.
Ignore the regulation and keep using profiles; fix it once someone complains, get the system running first.
Move all user data to servers in a region without GDPR to sidestep the regulation.
whenOtherWins: 如果用户已明确授权同意（consent）使用其数据，那在同意范围内的用户级特征仍可用，不必全退到上下文/cohort。
whenOtherWins_en: If users have given explicit consent, user-level features remain usable within that consent, so you needn't retreat entirely to contextual/cohort signals.
optionExplanations: 加密不改变「这是个人数据」的性质，GDPR 管的是收集和使用，不是存储形态，答偏了法律含义。
对；不依赖身份的上下文/群体信号 + 端上推理既保住可用性又合规，是标准的隐私适配。
「先违规跑起来」在受监管场景是重大风险，面试考的正是你会不会主动把合规当设计约束。
搬服务器绕监管是投机，用户所在地法规照样适用，且暴露严重合规与声誉风险。
optionExplanations_en: Encryption doesn't change that it's personal data; GDPR governs collection and use, not storage form, so this misreads the law.
Correct — identity-free contextual/cohort signals plus on-device inference keep the system usable and compliant, the standard privacy adaptation.
'Break the rules to ship' is a major risk in regulated settings; the interview tests whether you treat compliance as a design constraint.
Relocating servers to dodge regulation is opportunistic; the user's jurisdiction still applies, exposing serious compliance and reputation risk.

termDefinitions.meaning: 欧盟通用数据保护条例，要求用户同意与数据最小化，是设计约束不是可选项。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation) is the EU privacy law requiring consent and data minimization, a design constraint, not optional.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把相似用户聚成群、用群体层面的聚合行为做特征，不暴露单个用户身份。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cohort signal aggregates behavior over a group of similar users, giving features without exposing any individual identity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把模型推理放到用户设备本地运行，原始数据不离开设备，天然更合规。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: On-device inference runs the model locally on the user's device so raw data never leaves it, aiding compliance.

scenario: 面试官注入约束：团队从 15 人缩到 3 人。你原设计有多条复杂实时流水线，需要专人维护。
scenario_en: Constraint injected: the team shrinks from 15 to 3. Your design had several complex real-time pipelines needing dedicated upkeep.
q: 团队 15→3，复杂实时管线维护不了，怎么适配？
q_en: Team 15→3, complex real-time pipelines become unmaintainable — how do you adapt?
why: 小团队养不起多条实时流水线：改成批处理管线、多用托管服务（少自建）、降低模型更新频率。代价是新鲜度/实时适应性下降，但运维负担和 3 人团队匹配。
why_en: A small team can't run many real-time pipelines: switch to batch, lean on managed services, and update models less often, trading freshness for maintainability.
tradeoff: 批处理+托管服务+低频更新(省运维、新鲜度降) vs 实时自建管线(新鲜但3人养不起)
options: 让 3 个人加班干 15 个人的活，管线不变靠人力硬扛
把系统全部外包给外部供应商，自己团队什么都不碰
改批处理管线 + 多用托管服务 + 降低更新频率；代价是新鲜度/实时性下降但可维护
砍掉监控和告警省人力，出问题再救火，先保证核心链路跑着
options_en: Have 3 people work the hours of 15, keep the pipelines unchanged and brute-force it with overtime.
Outsource the entire system to an external vendor and have your team touch nothing.
Switch to batch pipelines + more managed services + lower update frequency; cost is reduced freshness/real-timeness but maintainable.
Cut monitoring and alerting to save headcount, firefight issues as they come, keep the core path running first.
whenOtherWins: 如果产品的核心价值就是实时性（如实时反欺诈、实时竞价），就不能退到批处理，得靠托管流式服务保住实时、用外部平台补人力缺口。
whenOtherWins_en: If real-timeness is the product's core value (real-time fraud, live bidding), you can't drop to batch — use managed streaming services to keep real-time while offsetting headcount.
optionExplanations: 靠加班硬扛不可持续，运维负担不随人力线性缩减，迟早在 3 人团队上崩掉。
全外包放弃了对核心系统的掌控，出问题无法快速响应，也不是「适配」而是逃避。
对；批处理+托管+低频更新把运维复杂度压到 3 人可承受，代价明说是新鲜度。
砍监控是拿可观测性换人力，反而让小团队在故障时更被动，是危险的省法。
optionExplanations_en: Overtime brute-forcing is unsustainable; ops burden doesn't shrink linearly with headcount and will collapse a 3-person team.
Full outsourcing gives up control of the core system and can't respond fast to incidents — evasion, not adaptation.
Correct — batch + managed + lower-frequency updates cut ops complexity to what 3 people can carry, with freshness as the stated cost.
Cutting monitoring trades observability for headcount, leaving a small team more helpless during incidents — a dangerous saving.

termDefinitions.meaning: 云厂商代运维的服务（如托管 Kafka、托管特征平台），换钱省掉自建和维护人力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A managed service is cloud-operated infrastructure (managed Kafka, feature platform), trading money for saved build-and-maintain headcount.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按周期(小时/天)成批处理数据，比实时流处理简单、运维成本低但新鲜度差。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A batch pipeline processes data in periodic bulk (hourly/daily), simpler and cheaper to run than streaming but less fresh.

scenario: 反欺诈系统，面试官把吞吐从 1k TPS 提到 100k TPS。当前每笔交易都同步算特征 + 同步调模型，延迟和成本瞬间爆炸。
scenario_en: A fraud system; the interviewer raises throughput from 1k to 100k TPS. Currently every transaction synchronously computes features and calls the model, blowing latency and cost.
q: 反欺诈 1k→100k TPS，同步逐笔打分扛不住，怎么适配？
q_en: Fraud 1k→100k TPS, synchronous per-transaction scoring can't cope — how do you adapt?
why: 上一个轻量规则预过滤，只把可疑交易路由给 ML 模型，其余走异步打分管线。代价是低信号欺诈的漏报率略升，但成本大幅下降、主路径不被 100k TPS 压垮。
why_en: Add a lightweight rule-based pre-filter routing only suspicious transactions to the ML model, with the rest scored asynchronously, trading a slightly higher false-negative rate for far lower cost.
tradeoff: 规则预过滤+异步打分(省成本、低信号漏报略升) vs 逐笔同步ML(准但100k TPS扛不住)
diagram:
flowchart LR
  T["交易 100k TPS"] --> P["轻量规则预过滤"]
  P -->|可疑| M["ML 模型打分"]
  P -->|其余| A["异步打分管线"]
options: 规则预过滤只把可疑交易送 ML + 其余异步打分；代价是低信号欺诈漏报略升，但成本大降
所有交易照旧同步逐笔调 ML 模型，只是把模型部署到更多 GPU 上
干脆停用 ML，全部用几条硬规则判欺诈，简单又扛得住吞吐
把每笔交易延迟处理，攒够一大批再统一打分，用户等结果没关系
options_en: Rule pre-filter routes only suspicious transactions to ML + the rest scored async; cost is slightly higher low-signal false negatives but far lower cost.
Keep scoring every transaction synchronously with the ML model, just deploy the model on more GPUs.
Drop ML entirely and judge fraud with a few hard rules — simple and handles the throughput.
Delay every transaction, batch a large group, and score them together; users waiting for a result is fine.
whenOtherWins: 如果每笔交易都必须实时同步给出放行/拒绝决定（如支付网关卡在同步路径上），就不能异步，得靠模型蒸馏+特征预计算在同步路径里提速。
whenOtherWins_en: If every transaction needs a real-time synchronous allow/deny decision (payment gateway on the sync path), you can't go async — speed up the sync path via distillation and precomputed features.
optionExplanations: 对；预过滤把绝大多数正常交易挡在 ML 之外，只精算可疑的，成本随之下降，漏报代价说清。
堆 GPU 是加钱不减负，100k TPS 下逐笔同步调 ML 的成本仍然爆炸，没解决根因。
纯规则扛得住吞吐但抓不住新型/复杂欺诈，召回大跌，把 ML 全砍是过度反应。
支付类决策通常要求近实时，攒大批延迟打分会让欺诈交易在判定前就完成，不可接受。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the pre-filter keeps most normal transactions away from ML and only finely scores suspicious ones, cutting cost with a stated false-negative tradeoff.
More GPUs spend more without reducing load; at 100k TPS synchronous per-transaction ML still explodes in cost, not fixing the root cause.
Pure rules handle throughput but miss novel/complex fraud, tanking recall; dropping ML entirely overreacts.
Payment decisions usually need near-real-time; batching with delayed scoring lets fraudulent transactions complete before judgment — unacceptable.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒事务数，衡量吞吐；100k TPS 意味着每秒要处理十万笔交易。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TPS (Transactions Per Second) measures throughput; 100k TPS means processing a hundred thousand transactions each second.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把真欺诈判成正常放过去，反欺诈里最危险的错误类型之一。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A false negative is letting a real fraud through as normal, one of the most dangerous error types in fraud detection.

termDefinitions.meaning: 不在请求同步路径上打分，交易先放行、后台再评估，牺牲即时性换吞吐。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Async scoring evaluates off the synchronous path — the transaction proceeds and is assessed in the background, trading immediacy for throughput.

scenario: 内容推荐系统，面试官说上线时只有 2 周数据（冷启动）。协同过滤(CF)所需的用户-物品交互信号太稀疏。
scenario_en: A content recommender; the interviewer says only 2 weeks of data at launch (cold start). The user-item interaction signals collaborative filtering needs are too sparse.
q: 冷启动只有 2 周数据、CF 信号太稀疏，怎么给出可用的 day-one 推荐？
q_en: Cold start with 2 weeks of data and sparse CF signals — how do you ship usable day-one recommendations?
why: CF 需要密集交互，冷启动给不了。改用基于内容的特征 + 预训练视觉模型给视频出 embedding + 热门度兜底。代价是初期个性化弱，但有可用的 day-one 体验，随数据积累再迁移到混合 CF。
why_en: CF needs dense interactions cold start can't give: use content-based features + pretrained-vision video embeddings + popularity fallback, trading early personalization for a usable day-one experience.
tradeoff: 内容特征+预训练embedding+热门兜底(day-one可用、个性化弱) vs 纯CF(个性化强但冷启动没信号)
options: 先等 3 个月攒够交互数据再上线，冷启动期间不做推荐
直接上纯 CF，信号稀疏就多跑几轮训练把它挤出来
基于内容特征 + 预训练视觉 embedding + 热门度兜底；初期个性化弱但 day-one 可用，后迁混合 CF
随机推荐，反正冷启动期用户也不知道什么是好推荐
options_en: Wait 3 months to accumulate interaction data before launching; make no recommendations during cold start.
Ship pure CF anyway; if signals are sparse, just run more training rounds to squeeze it out.
Content-based features + pretrained-vision embeddings + popularity fallback; weak early personalization but usable day-one, later migrate to hybrid CF.
Recommend randomly — during cold start users don't know what a good recommendation is anyway.
whenOtherWins: 如果上线时其实能拿到丰富的外部交互数据（如从关联产品迁移用户行为），就能更早用 CF，不必长期依赖内容兜底。
whenOtherWins_en: If rich external interaction data is available at launch (e.g. behavior migrated from a sister product), CF can kick in earlier without long reliance on content fallback.
optionExplanations: 等 3 个月不上线是把冷启动当借口逃避设计，产品要的是 day-one 就有可用体验。
CF 的病根是没交互信号，不是训练不够；稀疏数据再训也挤不出不存在的信号。
对；内容特征和预训练 embedding 不依赖交互历史，热门兜底保底线，正是冷启动标准解。
随机推荐白白浪费首批用户的留存机会，内容信号明明能给出比随机好得多的起点。
optionExplanations_en: Waiting 3 months uses cold start as an excuse to dodge design; the product needs a usable day-one experience.
CF's root problem is no interaction signal, not insufficient training; re-training sparse data can't squeeze out signal that doesn't exist.
Correct — content features and pretrained embeddings don't need interaction history, and popularity backstops it, the standard cold-start answer.
Random recommendations waste the first users' retention chance when content signals clearly give a far better starting point than random.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统或新用户/新物品缺乏历史交互数据的阶段，依赖交互的模型此时失效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cold start is when the system or a new user/item lacks historical interaction data, so interaction-dependent models fail.

termDefinitions.meaning: 协同过滤，靠「和你相似的用户喜欢什么」做推荐，需要密集的用户-物品交互。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CF (Collaborative Filtering) recommends via 'users like you liked X' and needs dense user-item interactions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 没有个性化信号时先推全局热门内容，保证冷启动期也有合理结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Popularity fallback serves globally popular items when no personalization signal exists, ensuring reasonable cold-start results.

scenario: 你为一个收紧的约束改出了更轻的设计，讲完适配方案就停下来等面试官反应。
scenario_en: You've reworked a lighter design for a tightened constraint and stop right after presenting the adaptation, waiting for the interviewer.
q: 提完适配方案，收尾还必须补一句什么？漏掉的后果是什么？
q_en: After presenting the adaptation, what one line must you add to close, and what's the cost of omitting it?
why: 补一句迁移路径：约束一旦放松，怎么回到原来的完整设计。原文明说漏掉迁移路径的候选人会被面试官注意到（负信号）——它证明你把适配当可演进工程，不是一次性妥协。
why_en: State the migration path back to the original design once the constraint relaxes; candidates who omit it get noticed as a negative signal.
options: 补一句「等约束放松后怎么迁回原设计」；漏掉会被面试官记为负信号
补一句自我表扬，强调这个适配方案有多巧妙
补一句让面试官下结论，把评判方案好坏的责任交给他
不用补，方案讲完就是完整答案，多说反而显得啰嗦
options_en: Add 'how to migrate back to the original design once the constraint relaxes'; omitting it is noted as a negative signal.
Add self-praise emphasizing how clever the adaptation is.
Add a prompt for the interviewer to conclude, handing them the job of judging the design.
No need — the solution as presented is complete, and saying more just sounds long-winded.
optionExplanations: 对；迁移路径证明你视约束为暂时的、方案是可逆的，正是资深候选人会主动补的收尾。
自我表扬不增加技术信息，面试官要的是可演进性论证不是形容词。
把评判交给面试官是回避，你自己应说清方案在约束放松后的演进方向。
漏掉迁移路径恰恰是原文点名的失分点，「多说啰嗦」在这里判断反了。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — a migration path shows you treat the constraint as temporary and the plan as reversible, the closing a senior candidate volunteers.
Self-praise adds no technical information; the interviewer wants an evolvability argument, not adjectives.
Handing judgment to the interviewer dodges it; you should state the design's evolution once the constraint relaxes.
Omitting the migration path is exactly the flagged failure; 'saying more is long-winded' has the judgment backwards here.

termDefinitions.meaning: 约束放松后从当前妥协方案回到原完整设计的演进计划，体现方案可逆可演进。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A migration path is the plan to evolve from the current compromise back to the full design once the constraint relaxes.

scenario: 面试官注入一个约束，候选人反过来论证这个约束不合理、坚持原设计不动，气氛开始紧张。
scenario_en: The interviewer injects a constraint; the candidate argues the constraint is unreasonable and refuses to budge, and tension rises.
q: 「死守原设计、跟约束较劲」是什么反模式，代价是什么？
q_en: What anti-pattern is 'defend the design, fight the constraint', and what's the cost?
why: 这叫 defensive spiral（防御螺旋）：死守被打破的设计、跟约束较劲，越辩越丢信任。原文说多数 pushback 失败是心态问题不是知识问题——问题不在你会不会，而在你肯不肯适应。
why_en: This is the defensive spiral — doubling down on a broken design and fighting the constraint, losing trust, since most pushback failures are mindset, not knowledge.
options: 这是聪明的坚持，坚守立场能让面试官觉得你有技术自信
这是 defensive spiral：死守坏设计、跟约束较劲、越辩越丢信任；多数失败是心态非知识
这只是沟通风格问题，与面试评分无关，把方案讲清就行
这是正常的技术辩论，约束本来就该被质疑到站不住为止
options_en: It's smart persistence; holding your ground makes the interviewer see technical confidence.
It's the defensive spiral: defending a broken design, fighting the constraint, losing trust — most failures are mindset, not knowledge.
It's just a communication-style issue, unrelated to scoring; explaining the design clearly is enough.
It's normal technical debate; constraints should be challenged until they collapse.
optionExplanations: 在给定约束下硬顶不是自信是僵化——面试官读到的是不肯适应，比会不会更致命。
对；defensive spiral 的核心代价是丢信任，改答案是重构不是认输，肯适应才是要考的信号。
它直接影响评分——adaptability 和 composure 正是明写的考察点，不是无关的风格。
约束是给定前提不是拿来推翻的靶子；把它辩倒等于拒绝题目本身，方向错了。
optionExplanations_en: Standing firm under a given constraint isn't confidence but rigidity — the interviewer reads unwillingness to adapt, more fatal than knowledge gaps.
Correct — the defensive spiral's core cost is lost trust; changing the answer is refactoring, not surrender, and adaptability is the tested signal.
It directly affects scoring — adaptability and composure are explicitly assessed, not an unrelated style matter.
The constraint is a given premise, not a target to overturn; arguing it down refuses the problem itself, the wrong direction.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面对 pushback 死守原设计、反驳约束，越辩越激化、越丢信任的失败反模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The defensive spiral is the failure pattern of clinging to the original design and arguing against the constraint, escalating and losing trust.

scenario: 约束一变，你意识到原设计不再是最优解，但担心改了会显得没主见、前后矛盾。
scenario_en: The constraint changes and you realize the original design is no longer optimal, but you worry that changing it looks indecisive or self-contradictory.
q: 约束变了、原设计不再最优，该坚持还是改？为什么？
q_en: Constraint changed and the original design is no longer optimal — hold or change, and why?
why: 该改。改答案不是软弱，是重构——约束变了，最优解本就该变。死守一个被打破的设计比果断转向信号更差；面试官看的是你能不能随证据调整。
why_en: Change it — updating your answer is refactoring, not weakness, since a changed constraint should change the optimum, and rigidly defending a broken design is a worse signal than pivoting.
tradeoff: 随约束调整设计(务实、显成熟) vs 死守原设计(显固执、信号更差)
options: 该改：改答案是重构不是软弱，死守被打破的设计信号更差
该坚持：改来改去显得没主见，坚定不动才显专业
该坚持：既然已经画了图，中途改会让前面的时间白费
都行：改不改无所谓，面试官只看你最初的方案
options_en: Change it: updating the answer is refactoring, not weakness, and defending a broken design is the worse signal.
Hold: changing back and forth looks indecisive; staying firm looks professional.
Hold: since you already drew the diagram, changing midway wastes the earlier time.
Either way: it doesn't matter — the interviewer only cares about your first design.
whenOtherWins: 如果新约束其实没有推翻原设计的核心前提（只是边角变化），就该守住并解释为什么原选择仍成立，而不是一被 push 就改。
whenOtherWins_en: If the new constraint doesn't actually break the original design's core premise (only a minor change), hold and explain why the choice still stands rather than changing at every push.
optionExplanations: 对；约束变则最优变，随证据调整是成熟不是善变，死守坏设计才是真正的失分。
把「不改」等同专业是误读——面试官要看适应力，僵化坚持读出的是扛不住追问。
沉没成本谬误：前面画的图是过程不是负担，为省它硬撑一个不再最优的设计更亏。
改不改恰恰影响评分，adaptability 是明写考察点，「只看最初方案」判断错了。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — a changed constraint changes the optimum; updating on evidence is maturity, not fickleness, while defending a broken design is the real loss.
Equating 'not changing' with professionalism misreads it — the interviewer wants adaptability, and rigidity reads as buckling under follow-ups.
Sunk-cost fallacy: the earlier diagram is process, not a burden, and clinging to a no-longer-optimal design to save it costs more.
Whether you change does affect scoring — adaptability is explicitly assessed, so 'only the first design matters' is wrong.

termDefinitions.term: refactoring vs defeat / 重构而非认输
termDefinitions.meaning: 把随约束调整设计理解为工程重构而不是承认失败，是面试该有的心态框架。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Reframing an adaptation as refactoring rather than admitting defeat is the mindset to hold in the interview.

scenario: 面试官抛出一个 pushback，你一时没想好完整答案，感到必须立刻开口的压力。
scenario_en: The interviewer throws a pushback and you don't yet have a full answer, feeling pressure to speak immediately.
q: 填空：面对 pushback 保持 composure 的做法。
q_en: Fill in: how to keep composure when facing pushback.
text: 被 pushback 不必秒答；说一句「{{让我想想这会改变什么}}」（约 {{5}} 秒）反而显成熟。{{沉默后给结构}} 胜过 {{求快后混乱}}。
text_en: You needn't answer instantly; a line like '{{let me think about what that changes}}' (about {{5}} seconds) reads as mature. {{Silence-then-structure}} beats {{speed-then-confusion}}.
why: 「让我想想」花约 5 秒买来结构化思考的空间，是成熟信号；面试官奖励的是有条理的适配，不是抢答的速度。慌忙求快反而暴露混乱。
why_en: A brief 'let me think about what that changes' buys structured-thinking space and reads as mature, since interviewers reward orderly adaptation over speed.

scenario: L5+ 的一场 ML 系统设计面试里，面试官在同一 session 注入了 2-3 个约束变更（先改延迟、再改数据量、再改团队规模）。
scenario_en: In one L5+ ML system design session, the interviewer injects 2-3 constraint changes (latency, then data volume, then team size).
q: 一场里连续被注入 2-3 个约束，正确的处理姿态是什么？
q_en: With 2-3 constraints injected in one session, what's the right way to handle them?
why: 把每个约束当成独立的结构化 mini-problem，逐个走同一套 4 步循环，而不是当成一次总崩溃慌乱应对。L5+ 常这样连环施压，正是在测你能不能稳定复用同一框架。
why_en: Treat each constraint as a separate structured mini-problem and run the same 4-step loop on each, rather than reacting to a session-wide crisis.
options: 把 2-3 个约束攒在一起，最后一次性重画一个能同时满足所有约束的大方案
第一个约束就重画整个系统，后面的约束到时候再看运气
把每个约束当独立的结构化 mini-problem，逐个走同一套 4 步循环
抗议约束太多不合理，请面试官一次只改一个
options_en: Batch the 2-3 constraints and redraw one big design at the end that satisfies them all at once.
Redraw the whole system on the first constraint and take the later ones as they come.
Treat each constraint as a separate structured mini-problem and run the same 4-step loop on each.
Protest that too many constraints is unfair and ask the interviewer to change only one.
optionExplanations: 攒到最后一次性解会丢掉每步的对齐机会，且约束间可能冲突，一锅端反而讲不清取舍。
第一个就全推倒是过度反应，后面「看运气」暴露没有可复用的方法，正是要避免的。
对；逐个当 mini-problem 走 4 步循环，展示的是稳定、可复用的结构化能力，正中考点。
抗议约束数量是另一种 defensive spiral，L5+ 连环施压本身就是考点，不能推回去。
optionExplanations_en: Batching to solve at the end loses each step's alignment chance, and constraints may conflict, muddling the tradeoffs.
Scrapping everything on the first is an overreaction, and 'take the rest as they come' shows no reusable method — exactly what to avoid.
Correct — handling each as a mini-problem through the 4-step loop shows stable, reusable structure, hitting the assessed skill.
Protesting the count is another defensive spiral; L5+ stacking pressure is the test itself and can't be pushed back.

termDefinitions.meaning: 资深/Staff 及以上级别，面试更强调在多重变化约束下稳定适配的能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: L5+ (Staff and above) levels emphasize stable adaptation under multiple shifting constraints.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一个约束变更当作一道独立的小设计题来结构化处理，而非整体危机。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A mini-problem treats each constraint change as its own small design task to handle structurally, not a total crisis.

scenario: 你提议用 GPU serving 跑推理，面试官说「只能用 CPU」。
scenario_en: You propose GPU serving for inference and the interviewer says 'CPUs only'.
q: 面试官改成「只能用 CPU」，用 4 步法怎么回应？
q_en: The interviewer switches to 'CPUs only' — how do you respond with the 4-step framework?
why: Acknowledge CPU 约束 → 指出为 GPU 优化的推理路径会坏（大模型在 CPU 上太慢）→ 提蒸馏/量化把算力压到 CPU 能扛 → 说清取舍（精度略降）。四步一气呵成正是被考的结构。
why_en: Acknowledge the CPU constraint, identify that GPU-optimized inference breaks, propose distillation/quantization to cut compute, and state the slight accuracy tradeoff.
tradeoff: 蒸馏/量化(CPU 上跑得动、精度略降) vs 原大模型(精度高但 CPU 扛不住)
options: 坚持要 GPU，向面试官解释为什么这个模型没 GPU 就是不行
Acknowledge CPU 约束→指出 GPU 推理坏了→提蒸馏/量化降算力→说清精度略降的取舍
把模型原封不动搬到 CPU 上，慢就慢点，用户多等一会没关系
换一个完全不同的任务，避开需要重推理的部分
options_en: Insist on GPUs and explain to the interviewer why this model just won't work without one.
Acknowledge the CPU constraint → note GPU inference breaks → propose distillation/quantization to cut compute → state the slight accuracy tradeoff.
Move the model to CPU unchanged; if it's slow, so be it — users can wait a bit.
Switch to a completely different task that avoids the heavy-inference part.
whenOtherWins: 如果模型本来就很小、CPU 完全跑得动，那不必蒸馏/量化，直接部署到 CPU 即可——过度压缩反而白丢精度。
whenOtherWins_en: If the model is already small and CPU-friendly, skip distillation/quantization and deploy on CPU directly — over-compressing just loses accuracy for nothing.
optionExplanations: 坚持要 GPU 是跟约束较劲的 defensive spiral，「只能 CPU」是给定前提不是可谈判的。
对；四步走完——认约束、点破坏处、给蒸馏/量化的适配、说代价，结构完整正中考点。
原样搬 CPU 会让大模型延迟爆炸，「慢点没关系」在有延迟 SLA 的服务里站不住。
换任务是逃避原题，面试官改的是硬件约束，要的是同一任务在 CPU 上的适配。
optionExplanations_en: Insisting on GPUs is a defensive spiral fighting the constraint; 'CPUs only' is a given premise, not negotiable.
Correct — all four steps: acknowledge, identify the break, propose distillation/quantization, state the cost; complete structure hits the assessed skill.
Moving a big model to CPU unchanged explodes latency; 'slow is fine' fails under any latency SLA.
Switching tasks dodges the problem; the interviewer changed hardware and wants the same task adapted to CPU.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把模型权重从 32 位浮点降到 8 位整数等低精度，减小体积、加速 CPU 推理，略损精度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Quantization lowers model weights from 32-bit float to lower precision like 8-bit int, shrinking size and speeding CPU inference with minor accuracy loss.

termDefinitions.term: GPU-optimized inference / GPU 优化推理
termDefinitions.meaning: 为并行硬件设计的大模型推理路径，搬到 CPU 上会因缺并行而严重变慢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GPU-optimized inference is a large-model path built for parallel hardware; on CPU it slows badly for lack of parallelism.

scenario: 面试官质疑你的某个具体技术选择（「你为什么用 Kafka 而不是 Kinesis？」）——这是 decision challenge，不是改约束。
scenario_en: The interviewer questions a specific choice ('why Kafka not Kinesis?') — a decision challenge, not a constraint change.
q: 面对 decision challenge（质疑具体选择），该怎么回应？
q_en: Facing a decision challenge (a questioned choice), how do you respond?
why: 讲清当初权衡的取舍轴，以及为什么在这些约束下这么选（如 Kafka 的分区/消费组灵活性 vs Kinesis 的 AWS 托管便利），证明这是想过的选择不是随手默认。这与「改约束」要走的 4 步适配不同。
why_en: Explain the tradeoff axis you weighed and why this choice fits the given constraints, proving it was a considered decision rather than a default.
tradeoff: 讲清选择的取舍轴(证明想过) vs 改约束走4步适配(两类pushback回应不同)
options: 立刻改用 Kinesis，面试官既然问了肯定是觉得 Kafka 不对
说「这是行业标准做法」，用惯例搪塞过去不展开
承认自己也不确定，把选择权交还给面试官让他定
讲清当初权衡的取舍轴 + 为什么在这些约束下这么选，证明是想过的选择
options_en: Immediately switch to Kinesis — since they asked, they must think Kafka is wrong.
Say 'it's the industry-standard approach' and deflect with convention without elaborating.
Admit you're not sure and hand the choice back to the interviewer to decide.
Explain the tradeoff axis you weighed and why this choice fits the given constraints, proving it was considered.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官同时改了约束（比如「现在全栈都在 AWS 上」），那这其实是 constraint injection，就该走 4 步适配、可能真的换 Kinesis，而非只辩护原选择。
whenOtherWins_en: If the interviewer also changed a constraint (e.g. 'everything is on AWS now'), it's actually constraint injection — run the 4-step loop and possibly switch to Kinesis, not just defend Kafka.
optionExplanations: 一问就改暴露的正是随手默认、没想清取舍，恰恰是 decision challenge 要抓的软肋。
「行业标准」是零信息搪塞，面试官要的是你自己的权衡逻辑不是诉诸惯例。
把选择权推回去等于承认没想过，decision challenge 考的就是你能否讲清 why。
对；说清取舍轴和适配约束的理由，证明这是深思熟虑的选择，正面回应了质疑。
optionExplanations_en: Switching on the first ask reveals exactly a default with no reasoning — the soft spot a decision challenge targets.
'Industry standard' is a zero-information deflection; the interviewer wants your own tradeoff logic, not an appeal to convention.
Handing the choice back admits you didn't reason it; a decision challenge tests whether you can articulate the why.
Correct — laying out the tradeoff axis and why it fits the constraints proves a deliberate choice, meeting the challenge head-on.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两种分布式消息流平台：Kafka 分区/消费组更灵活、自建；Kinesis 是 AWS 托管、集成便利但灵活性略低。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka and Kinesis are streaming platforms: Kafka offers more partitioning/consumer flexibility (self-run), Kinesis is AWS-managed and convenient but less flexible.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两个方案真正区别开的那一维（如灵活性 vs 托管便利），讲清它才算真懂选择。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A tradeoff axis is the dimension that truly separates two options (flexibility vs managed convenience); naming it proves you understand the choice.

scenario: 内容推荐冷启动：上线只有 2 周数据，要给出一条从「无信号」到「可演进」的完整推理链。
scenario_en: Content-rec cold start: only 2 weeks of data at launch; give a full reasoning chain from 'no signal' to 'evolvable'.
q: 把冷启动适配的决策链排成正确顺序（需求→缺陷→选择→兜底→迁移）：
q_en: Order the cold-start adaptation decision chain (requirement → gap → choice → fallback → migration):
steps: 识别缺陷：CF 需要密集用户-物品交互，冷启动信号太稀疏
承认约束：上线只有 2 周数据，必须给出 day-one 可用推荐
迁移路径：随交互数据积累，逐步切到混合 CF
加兜底：用全局热门度兜底，保证冷门场景也有结果
选替代：改用内容特征 + 预训练视觉 embedding，不依赖交互历史
why: 链条：承认 2 周数据约束 → 认清 CF 因信号稀疏失效 → 改用不依赖交互的内容/预训练 embedding → 热门度兜底保底线 → 数据积累后迁回混合 CF。每一步都为下一步的选择提供依据。
why_en: Acknowledge the 2-week constraint, see CF fails on sparse signal, switch to interaction-free content/pretrained embeddings, backstop with popularity, then migrate to hybrid CF as data grows.
diagram:
flowchart LR A["承认约束
2周数据"] --> B["CF 失效
信号稀疏"] B --> C["内容+预训练embedding"] C --> D["热门度兜底"] D --> E["迁移: 混合 CF"]

termDefinitions.term: hybrid CF / 混合协同过滤
termDefinitions.meaning: 把协同过滤与内容特征结合的推荐方法，数据积累后可从纯内容方案平滑迁移过去。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hybrid CF combines collaborative filtering with content features, a smooth migration target once interaction data accumulates.

scenario: 复盘一场被 pushback 打崩的面试：候选人技术其实都会，但一被追问就慌、防御、越描越乱。
scenario_en: Debriefing an interview that collapsed under pushback: the candidate knew the material but panicked, got defensive, and made it worse under follow-ups.
q: 多数 pushback 失败的根因是什么？这对练习重点意味着什么？
q_en: What's the root cause of most pushback failures, and what does it imply for practice?
why: 根因是心态不是知识——多数人不是不会适配，而是慌乱、防御、跟约束较劲。所以练习重点应放在「稳定走完 4 步循环」而不是每次适配是否「最优」，结构本身才是被奖励的。
why_en: The root cause is mindset, not knowledge, so practice should focus on stably running the 4-step loop rather than on whether each adaptation is optimal.
options: 根因是知识不够，应该多背各种适配方案的标准答案
根因是心态不是知识；练习该练「稳定走完 4 步循环」，结构本身被奖励
根因是运气，遇到什么 pushback 全看面试官心情，练不了
根因是速度太慢，应该练秒答，越快越显得强
options_en: The root cause is insufficient knowledge; memorize standard answers for every adaptation.
The root cause is mindset, not knowledge; practice running the 4-step loop stably — the structure itself is rewarded.
The root cause is luck; which pushback you get is up to the interviewer's mood and can't be practiced.
The root cause is being too slow; practice instant answers — faster looks stronger.
optionExplanations: 背标准答案治不了慌乱，真实约束千变万化，背得再多一进防御状态照样崩。
对；既然瓶颈在心态，练习就该练稳定复用 4 步结构，而非追求每次适配的「正确性」。
把失败归给运气就放弃了可练的部分——4 步循环恰恰是可反复演练的稳定框架。
求快正是制造混乱的原因之一，面试奖励的是结构化不是抢答速度。
optionExplanations_en: Memorizing answers doesn't cure panic; real constraints vary endlessly, and even well-memorized, a defensive state still collapses.
Correct — since the bottleneck is mindset, practice reusing the 4-step structure stably rather than chasing each adaptation's 'correctness'.
Blaming luck abandons the practicable part — the 4-step loop is exactly a stable framework you can rehearse repeatedly.
Chasing speed is a cause of the chaos; the interview rewards structure, not buzzer speed.

termDefinitions.term: mindset over knowledge / 心态优先
termDefinitions.meaning: pushback 面试里冷静复用框架的心态比掌握更多方案更决定成败。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: In pushback interviews, the composed mindset of reusing a framework decides outcomes more than knowing more solutions.
